brief: 8 mistakes I made as a first-time founder that cost me $250K.

slots.title: 1. Hiring Too Fast
slots.body: I hired five people before validating demand. Payroll burned $18K monthly while revenue stayed flat. Hire only after traction is undeniable.

slots.title: 2. No Customer Calls
slots.body: I spent six months building features nobody wanted. Talk to ten prospects before writing a single line of production code.

slots.title: 3. Paid Ads Too Early
slots.body: I burned $40K on Instagram ads for a leaky funnel. Fix conversion and retention before you spend a dollar on acquisition.

slots.title: 4. Ignoring Burn Rate
slots.body: I mixed personal and business funds with zero budget tracking. Know your exact runway every Monday morning without exception.

slots.title: 5. Shipping Too Late
slots.body: I rewrote the stack three times chasing perfect architecture. Launch an embarrassing MVP in weeks, not a polished product in months.

slots.title: 6. Yes To Everyone
slots.body: I built custom features for every enterprise prospect. One-off requests killed our roadmap. Learn to say no early.
